problems.title: Compaction by hand
problems.solution: Flags [1, 0, 1, 0, 1, 1, 0, 0], exclusive scan [0, 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 4, 4]: 7 (index 5) goes to 3. Output [5, 8, 3, 7], length 4.

problems.title: Passes
problems.statement: LSD radix sort of 32-bit keys with d-bit digits.
problems.solution: 4, 8 and 3. With d = 11 the last pass covers only 10 bits; some sorts use 11-bit digits to save a pass at the cost of 2,048-bin histograms.

problems.title: Sort traffic
problems.statement: Sort $2^{24}$ 32-bit keys with 8-bit digits on the GW-1.

parts.prompt: Straightforward passes (3n accesses each): total bytes?
Onesweep (one histogram pass reading n, then 2n per digit pass): time bound, in ms?

problems.solution: (a) $4 \times 3 \times 2^{24} \times 4 = 805,306,368$ bytes, (b) 1.57 ms. (c) $9n$ accesses: 1.18 ms, 1.33× less traffic.

problems.title: Tracing LSD radix sort
problems.statement: Sort [13, 6, 9, 2] with 2-bit digits (base 4), least significant first, stably.

parts.prompt: After the first pass, the position (0-based) of 6?
After the first pass, the position of 9?

problems.solution: First pass (by low digit, stable): [13, 9, 6, 2]. Second pass by the high digit (13 → 3, 9 → 2, 6 → 1, 2 → 0): [2, 6, 9, 13]. Stability kept 13 before 9 after pass one; pass two then fixed their order by the high digit.

problems.title: The digit-tile table
problems.statement: Two tiles, 2-bit digits. Counts per digit: tile 0 [2, 1, 0, 1], tile 1 [1, 0, 3, 0]. Scan the table in digit-major order.
problems.solution: Offsets: (d0,t0)=0, (d0,t1)=2, (d1,t0)=3, (d1,t1)=4, (d2,t0)=4, (d2,t1)=4, (d3,t0)=7, (d3,t1)=8. Digit-major order puts all digit-0 keys first, and within a digit, tile 0's before tile 1's, which preserves stability across tiles.

problems.title: Ranks from a ballot
problems.statement: A ballot of lanes whose digit equals d returns the mask 0xb275ad35 (bit ℓ for lane ℓ). Lane 13 is in it.

parts.prompt: Lane 13's rank among those lanes (number of set bits below bit 13)?

problems.solution: Bits 0–12 of the mask: 0110100110101 → 7 set, so rank 7. The group has 18 lanes. One ballot and one popcount give every lane its stable position within the warp.

problems.title: Sorting floats as integers
problems.statement: Radix sort works on unsigned bit patterns.

options: flip the sign bit of every float
flip the sign bit of positives, all bits of negatives

parts.prompt: Why flip all bits of negatives?
options: Larger negative magnitudes have larger bit patterns, so their order must be reversed

hints: Compare the bit patterns of −1.0 and −2.0.
problems.solution: Positives already order correctly as unsigned once the sign bit is set (putting them above negatives). Negative floats are sign-magnitude: −2.0's pattern is larger than −1.0's, so inverting all their bits reverses that order and clears the sign bit.

problems.title: Sorting fat records
problems.statement: Sort $10^7$ records of 64 bytes by a 32-bit key with 4 radix passes, each moving every element twice (read and write).

parts.prompt: Bytes moved sorting the records directly (keys and payloads)?
Sorting (key, 32-bit index) pairs, then one gather of the records (read 64, write 64 each)?

problems.solution: (a) 5.44 GB. (b) 1.92 GB: 2.8× less. Sort handles, not records.

problems.title: Stable or fast
problems.statement: Compact $2^{24}$ floats keeping half. Scan-based (stable): one pass reads all to count, a second reads all and writes the kept. Atomic-based (unordered): one pass reads all and writes the kept. Ignore the small scan and the atomics' cost.
problems.solution: (a) $2.5n \times 4$ = 168 MB, (b) $1.5n \times 4$ = 101 MB, (c) 1.67×. A single-pass scan (look-back) closes the gap and stays stable; that's what CUB's DeviceSelect does.

problems.title: How big a digit?
problems.statement: Per-tile histograms live in shared memory (48 KB per block on the GW-1), 4-byte counters.

parts.prompt: Bytes for one histogram with d = 8?

options: No: the histogram is 5× bigger than a block's shared memory, and mostly empty for small tiles

problems.solution: 1 KB versus 256 KB. Large digits save passes but make histograms (and the digit-tile table) huge and sparse. 8 bits is the sweet spot on current GPUs.
